description: Exchange Triage extraction prompts v1, v2 and v3 over the 27-case golden set, through the production pipeline (intake, extraction, grounding, appetite; writer off) on claude sonnet via the CLI. Baseline v2 (what shipped 2026-07-27), candidate v3 (production), v2-repeat as the noise floor, v1 as the frozen plain prompt. Reference: the golden labels. Judges: two source-attribution classifiers, validated against human labels in suites/exchange-triage.labels.jsonl.

variants.name: v2
variants.description: Extraction prompt v2: canonical construction classes and the broker-working-value rule. Shipped 2026-07-27.

variants.name: v2-repeat
variants.description: v2 run a second time on identical inputs: the noise floor.

variants.name: v3
variants.description: Extraction prompt v3, production: null-first subclass rule and source tied to a citable span, after a live over-extraction Arize caught.

variants.name: v1
variants.description: Extraction prompt v1, frozen: plain instructions, no construction mapping, no few-shot examples.

checks.description: Extraction JSON matched the schema within the pipeline's two attempts.
Every labelled field matches the golden value under the app's own field scorer (0.5% on dollar amounts, canonical construction class, null means null).
constructionType is the canonical ISO class the appetite rules consume, not the broker's wording.
Fields the source never states come back null (no guessed TIV, year built, state or subclass).
The routing decision matches the golden label.
Jev (TypeSafe yes/no classifier) says every `source` attribution is truthful: the value is stated in the document it names. Pass at probability 0.5 or above.
Claude Haiku, given only the source text and the extracted fields, says every `source` attribution is truthful.
